questions.q: Who is the protagonist in "The Wild Swans at Coole," and what is his primary role in the poem?
questions.a: The protagonist is the first-person speaker, identified with the poet W.B. Yeats himself. His role is to observe the swans, reflect on the passage of nineteen years, and embody the human condition of aging and loss in contrast to the swans' apparent timelessness. A wrong answer (e.g., "the swans are the protagonist") reveals confusion between the subject of observation and the observing consciousness — a fundamental error in lyric poetry analysis.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what the speaker means by "All's changed since I, hearing at twilight, / The first time on this shore, / The bell-beat of their wings above my head, / Trod with a lighter tread."
questions.a: The speaker recalls his first visit nineteen years earlier when he walked ("trod") with a "lighter tread" — meaning he was younger, less burdened by sorrow or awareness of mortality. Now, hearing the same "bell-beat" of wings, he feels the weight of time ("All's changed"). A wrong answer that focuses only on the physical walk or misses the temporal comparison shows inability to infer emotional state from metaphorical language.

questions.q: Apply the concept of "contrast" to analyze how the protagonist's character is revealed in stanza 3 ("Unwearied still, lover by lover..."). Write two specific contrasts between the speaker and the swans.
questions.a: Contrast 1: The swans are "unwearied" and "their hearts have not grown old"; the speaker's heart is "sore" and he has aged across "nineteen autumns." Contrast 2: The swans' passion and conquest "attend upon them still" wherever they wander; the speaker is stationary, bound to the shore, fearing they will "fly away." A wrong answer that lists only physical differences (e.g., swans fly, man walks) misses the psychological and existential contrast central to the protagonist's portrayal.

questions.q: Analyze how the poem's structure (five stanzas, consistent rhyme scheme, shifting focus) mirrors the protagonist's mental movement from observation to personal reflection to future dread.
questions.a: Stanzas 1–2 move from objective description (trees, water, swans) to personal history ("The nineteenth autumn has come upon me"). Stanza 3 contrasts the swans' permanence with human transience. Stanza 4 shifts to present stillness ("drift on the still water") and mystery. Stanza 5 projects future loss ("when I awake some day / To find they have flown away"). The structure enacts the protagonist's mind: observation → memory → contrast → present awareness → anticipatory grief. A wrong answer that merely describes stanzas without linking to the speaker's psychological arc shows inability to connect form to character.

questions.q: Evaluate the claim: "The protagonist in this poem is passive; he only watches and does not act." Defend or refute with evidence.
questions.a: Refute. The protagonist's "action" is the act of counting, remembering, comparing, and articulating — all mental acts that constitute the poem itself. His counting ("made my count") is deliberate; his heart becoming "sore" is an emotional response; his final question ("Among what rushes will they build...?") is an imaginative projection. In lyric poetry, consciousness is action. A wrong answer agreeing with passivity confuses physical inactivity with poetic agency, missing that the speaker's perception shapes the entire meaning.

questions.q: Create a four-line stanza in the voice of the protagonist ten years after the poem's setting, maintaining the same rhyme scheme (ABCBDD) and meter, expressing his continued vigil at Coole.
questions.a: Example: "The twenty-ninth autumn finds me here again, / The woodland paths are dry and strewn with gold, / I count the swans — but nine-and-fifty remain, / Their wings still bell-beat on the water cold. / My heart is heavier, my tread more slow, / Yet still they paddle where the rushes grow." A poor answer would ignore the rhyme scheme, meter, or the protagonist's established voice (melancholy, precise counting, contrast with swans), revealing inability to internalize the persona.
